nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose boolean equality test agrees with equality, let $x$ and $y$ be lists over $\alpha$, and let $(k, w)$ be the pair returned by the dynamic-programming longest common subsequence algorithm on $x$ and $y$. Then $w$ has length $k$, $w$ is a subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) of both $x$ and $y$, and every common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ has length at most the length of $w$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the longest common subsequence algorithm

nodes.summary: For lists $x$ and $y$ of lengths $m$ and $n$ over a type with a boolean equality test, the abstract time of the dynamic-programming longest common subsequence algorithm on $x$ and $y$ (its number of table and reconstruction transitions) is at most $mn + (m + n)$.
nodes.title: Running time of the longest common subsequence algorithm

nodes.summary: Given lists $x = x_1 \cdots x_m$ and $y = y_1 \cdots y_n$ over a type with a boolean equality test, fill a table $c_{i,j}$ for $0 \le i \le m$ and $0 \le j \le n$ by $c_{i,0} = c_{0,j} = 0$, by $c_{i,j} = c_{i-1,j-1} + 1$ when the test reports $x_i = y_j$, and by $c_{i,j} = \max(c_{i-1,j}, c_{i,j-1})$ otherwise. conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.
